setup_summary.text: Q3 2026 was the company's highest sales quarter ever, per the CEO, but the stock fell about 7–9% on the Q4 guide. Sales and revenues were $20.682B (+17%) on $2.2B of higher sales volume. Adjusted EPS was $7.20 against $4.95 a year ago, and adjusted operating margin was 20.6%. Management guided only 'moderate' Q4 sales growth, saying Q4 2025 is a tough comparison.

Q3 was flattered by IEEPA tariff recoveries. Operating profit included $128M of recoveries, after $392M in Q2, so about $520M year to date. Management assumes none in Q4. On my arithmetic, $128M is about $0.21 of EPS at a 23% tax rate and about 461M diluted shares. Excluding it, Q3 EPS was about $6.99 against the $7.16 consensus quoted by AlphaStreet, if that consensus excluded recoveries. That basis is unknown.

The full-year guide is unchanged: sales growth in the mid-to-high teens, and adjusted operating margin 'near the bottom of the target range' excluding IEEPA recoveries. Tariffs are about $2.2B, with about $600M in Q4. Management also guides restructuring costs to about $300M and capex to about $3.3B, down from $3.5B.

Q4 2025 revenue was about $19.133B (full-year $67.589B less nine months $48.456B). At 15–19% full-year growth, Q4 would be $19.1–21.8B, and 17% gives $20.44B. 'Moderate' growth is undefined by management. On my 5–10% assumption it implies $20.1–21.05B. My base is about $20.6B (+7.5%), versus the $21.65B in the consensus feed (+13%) and the $21.42B pre-call consensus quoted by management (+12%).

My Q4 adjusted EPS base is about $6.55, in a range of about $6.1–6.9. It assumes a 19.0% adjusted margin, other income roughly offsetting interest, a 23% tax rate and about 459M diluted shares. That is about 8% below the $7.08 consensus. Revenue looks the clearer miss risk; EPS is high only if $7.08 is the live number. Each 25bp of margin is about $0.09 of EPS.

The fact sheet's consensus growth rates (+22.7% revenue, +45.1% EPS for Q4) use Q3 2025 as the prior-year base, so do not rely on F.70 and F.72. Q4 2025 revenue was about $19.133B (FY2025 $67.589B less nine-month $48.456B), so consensus revenue of $21.65B is about +13%. Q4 2025 GAAP diluted EPS is roughly $5.12 (FY $18.81 less nine-month $13.69; per-share figures are not strictly additive), which would make consensus EPS of $7.08 about +38%. That EPS comparison is approximate and may mix GAAP and adjusted bases.

Valuation still demands growth. TIKR says CAT traded at 25x forward earnings at Wednesday's close, 'lower still' on Oct 29, against a five-year average of 19x. It puts the stock 38% below its June 30 high. 2026 consensus EPS is $27.33 (up from $24.72 90 days ago) and the Street average target is about $939, with a range of $575–1,150. After the print, UBS cut its target to $750, Bernstein to $749 and Wells Fargo to $840.

Cash returns and working capital: Q3 MP&E free cash flow was $3.8B, with $1.2B of buybacks and about $0.7B of dividends. Enterprise cash was $7.9B (from $10.0B at year-end). Inventories rose to $22.2B (from $18.1B), receivables to $13.4B (from $10.9B) and customer advances to $5.3B (from $3.3B).

since_filing.text: The Q3 print came on Oct 29 and the stock fell about 7–9%. Stocktwits had it 9.5% lower premarket, Tradingkey 8.36% down, and 24/7 Wall St 7%. Drivers cited were the 'moderate' Q4 guide against a pre-call revenue consensus of $21.42B and a high starting multiple. AlphaStreet's piece describes the market reaction as 'muted', which conflicts with the other accounts; the sources here do not explain the difference.

Target cuts, mostly before the Oct 29 print, and a stress signal on AI funding. Wells Fargo cut its target to $840 from $1,155 on Oct 26, citing mounting stress around AI funding. UBS went to $750 and Bernstein to $749 in October cuts (exact dates not given). Oppenheimer reiterated Outperform with a $1,009 target on the day of the report (cut from $1,118 on Oct 14). Treasury yields hit 24-year highs in early October. These are TIKR's summary, not primary notes.

The consensus feed may be stale. The press quotes a pre-call revenue consensus of $21.42B, and the feed shows $21.65B and EPS of $7.08, higher than that. A 'moderate' Q4 guide should have lowered estimates. I treat $21.65B and $7.08 as unconfirmed on date and basis, and expect downward revisions toward about $20.5–21.4B and EPS of about $6.4–6.9 if they are pre-print.

Two items offset in the Q3 consensus. TIKR notes 2026 consensus EPS rose to $27.33 from $24.72 over 90 days, while 2027 moved to about $33 from about $30. It argues the softer Q4 is unlikely to pull 2027 down, but the January guide on margin is the swing factor.

IEEPA refunds: CAPE Phase 3, for finally liquidated entries, opened Oct 27 for plaintiffs with court-ordered relief; filing a lawsuit alone does not establish eligibility. Whether Caterpillar qualifies is not disclosed. Caterpillar records recoveries only for claims submitted and accepted through CAPE ($392M in Q2, about $520M year to date through Q3). As of June 30 it did not deem the remaining amounts probable, and its outlook includes no further IEEPA recoveries in Q4. Against roughly $1.0B of total IEEPA costs, that implies about $480M unrecovered (our arithmetic, not a company figure).

Peer read-through is supportive for power. GE Vernova's Q3 gas-turbine orders were 16.6 GW versus 7.4 GW a year earlier, and its Power RPO was $130.9B. Generac reported a data-center backlog that tripled to $4.5B, and its CEO said competitors including Caterpillar are adding capacity to sell existing products. Cummins' Q2 filing showed Power Systems sales +19% and power generation +27%, attributed to higher demand in China and North America (the data-center driver was cited for its Distribution segment); its Q3 results were not available.

Data-center funding and build risk is a live debate. A SemiAnalysis-based article on Oct 29 cites permitting delays, local opposition, interconnection, labor shortages and power-equipment backlogs as limits on the buildout, with one skeptic seeing about 25 GW rather than 50 GW. CAT management says it has not seen significant changes in how customers are placing or timing orders.

Resource Industries leadership changed. Derrick York succeeded Denise Johnson as RI Group President effective Nov 1, 2026. The CEO said he has worked closely with York for well over a decade. Separately, the CEO described the RI capacity ramp as 'normal growing pains and operational challenges'.

Mining demand inputs are supportive. Copper was about $14,379/t on Oct 29 and the World Bank raised its 2027 copper outlook 18% to $13,000/t. Freeport guided Q4 sales volumes to be the highest of the year. A counter-signal: Eldorado Gold cut 2026 guidance 18% on commissioning delays at Skouries.

key_debates.question: Is the 'moderate' Q4 guide conservative, or is the Street still too high on revenue and EPS?

bull.text: Management says Q3 matched its plan and it 'hasn't changed its view' on Q4. The weaker year-on-year Q4 is a comparison and timing story: a $1.6B CI destock against $0.6B last year, a strong Q4 2025, and no slack in P&E capacity. Backlog at $78B and 58% shipping within 12 months support 2027. The CI destock leaves year-end dealer inventory higher than a year ago.

bear.text: Arithmetic puts Q4 revenue at about $20.6B and adjusted EPS at about $6.55, below the $21.65B and $7.08 in the feed. Q4 2025 revenue is about $19.133B, so consensus implies about +13% against management's 'moderate'. Revenue of $21.65B needs full-year growth near the top of the mid-to-high-teens guide, and Q4 carries no IEEPA benefit.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Jan 27 print versus a fresh post-print consensus. First confirm whether $21.65B and $7.08 are the live numbers, since the pre-call figure was $21.42B. Then check Q4 revenue near $20.6B versus above $21.4B, and whether the adjusted margin is near 19% or above 19.5%.

key_debates.question: Is Power & Energy capacity-limited or is demand slowing as orders extend to 2029–2030?

bull.text: Power generation sales to users rose 75% in Q3 and P&E sales grew 18% with a 24.4% margin. Management says capacity is the top pacing factor, with large reciprocating engine capacity going to nearly three times the 2024 level by 2030, and a second 3600-series line planned at Winston-Salem. GE Vernova's orders and RPO and Generac's backlog confirm the end demand.

bear.text: An analyst put book-to-bill at about 1.3, down from as high as 1.7. Backlog growth slowed to about $6B (about $78B versus $72.1B at June 30) from $9.4B in Q2. Orders now run to 2029–2030, which the CEO calls unusual. Q4 P&E guidance is only 'moderate'. Prime-power and mining orders will come in lumps. Third-party commentary cites AI-funding stress, permitting delays, grid interconnection, labor shortages and power-equipment backlogs as limits on the data-center buildout.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 P&E sales versus an estimated $8.8–9.7B, Q4 backlog and book-to-bill, any cancellation or push-out commentary, and the 2027 capacity ramp (the 10-megawatt MaK restart starts shipping in Q4).

key_debates.question: How much of the margin is underlying, and can it move off the bottom of the target range?

bull.text: Underlying adjusted margin was about 20% in both Q2 and Q3 excluding IEEPA. Management guides a higher margin than Q4 2025 and wants to move toward the midpoint over a couple of years. Price realization was $663M in Q3, and the target range is progressive in sales. Sales growth should add operating leverage.

bear.text: Management itself guides the full year to near the bottom of the range excluding IEEPA, and the CEO says margins are 'skipping along the bottom'. Freight on elevated energy prices, capacity-expansion depreciation, tariffs of about $2.2B and higher SG&A/R&D are headwinds. Recoveries flatter reported results: $520M year to date, and the Q3 recovery fell about two-thirds from Q2.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 adjusted margin excluding any recoveries, compared with about 19% (my base) and the roughly 19.4% implied by consensus, and the January 2027 guide: does it place the margin above the bottom of the range?

key_debates.question: Can Resource Industries deliver a Q4 catch-up while ramping large mining trucks?

bull.text: RI orders have been strong for three quarters, copper and gold are supportive, and management expects Q3 commissioning delays to catch up, with strong Q4 growth. The year-ago comparison for mining sales to users is easy (Q4 2025 total RI STU down 5%).

bear.text: RI was the one segment to miss in Q3 (sales to users +4%, below expectations), with operational challenges and inefficiencies in the ramp and no timeline. Rail is a drag against a hard comparison (Q4 2025 rail sales to users up 26%) and locomotive deliveries are now guided slightly lower for the year. A new Group President takes over during the ramp.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 RI sales versus about $4.9–5.1B on the guide, RI sales to users in the Jan 27 retail statistics, RI margin versus 13.5% in Q3, and any sizing of the delayed commissioning.

key_debates.question: Does the multiple leave room for a guidance-driven reaction?

bull.text: Earnings estimates keep rising (2026 consensus $27.33, up from $24.72; 2027 about $33 from about $30), the Street target is about $939 and Oppenheimer's is $1,009. Buybacks at lower prices mechanically lift EPS.

bear.text: The stock still trades near 24x forward on the $27.33 estimate (if the price is about $645–655) versus a 19x five-year average. TIKR says Oppenheimer's target implies about 35x and needs a premium multiple to hold. The Q3 reaction of about 7–9% was roughly twice the ±4.7% average earnings move.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The 2027 outlook in the Jan 27 report, and especially whether margin guidance moves off the bottom of the range, plus post-print estimate revisions.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: Q4 revenue of about $21.4B or more (+12% or more), adjusted margin of about 19.5% or higher, and adjusted EPS near $7.0 or above. This needs a faster P&E ramp, a full RI commissioning catch-up, and stronger CI sales to users than the guide. Any IEEPA recoveries would add on top: $128M is about $0.21 of EPS. The 2027 commentary would point to margins moving off the bottom of the range.

triggers: P&E sales near $9.5B or more with Q3-like margin
RI sales of $5B or more and mining sales to users rebounding
CI sales to users staying near +15–20% despite the destock
New CAPE Phase 3 recoveries booked in Q4
2027 margin guidance above the bottom of the target range

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Q4 revenue of about $20.6B (+7.5%), adjusted margin of about 19.0%, and adjusted EPS of about $6.55, about 8% below the $7.08 in the feed. Backlog grows again but unevenly, MP&E free cash flow lands in the top half of the range, and buybacks continue at about $1.2B a quarter. The stock reacts to the 2027 framework more than to the quarter.

triggers: CI sales flat with a $1.6B destock
P&E up moderately with margin near Q3's 24%
RI sales growth in the mid-teens
2027 commentary reiterating strong sales to users and capacity ramp

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Q4 revenue of about $20.1B (+5%) with the adjusted margin at 18% or lower and EPS of about $5.5–6.1. Freight and capacity-expansion costs bite, the RI ramp slips again, and backlog or book-to-bill softens, which would hit a stock still trading at a premium multiple. A 16–18% margin would conflict with the guided Q3-like P&E margin, so I treat the lower end as the tail.

triggers: RI sales growth under 10% as the catch-up slips
CI sales down on a larger destock or fading rental loading
Order push-outs or a backlog decline in P&E
Freight and material inflation above plan
Cautious 2027 margin guide with AI-funding concerns weighing on the multiple

claim.text: CI dealer destock and rental fleet-loading fade. A $1.6B Q4 drawdown against $0.6B a year ago is a roughly $1B volume headwind. Rental loading will contribute less to sales-to-users growth than in Q3 as it laps strong Q4 2025 loading, and management gives no dollar size for it.

Data-center and AI-funding sustainability. P&E growth leans on power generation (sales to users +75%). Permitting, interconnection, labor and equipment bottlenecks and mounting stress around AI funding are being flagged, and orders now stretch to 2029–2030.

Margin stuck near the bottom of the range. Freight (elevated energy prices), capacity-expansion depreciation, SG&A/R&D and about $2.2B of tariffs offset price and volume. An 18% Q4 margin would put EPS near $6.1.

Resource Industries ramp and commissioning. Large mining truck ramp challenges, mining commissioning delays, and lower locomotive deliveries led to the only segment miss in Q3. The segment is also under a new Group President.

Quality of earnings: IEEPA recoveries ($392M in Q2, $128M in Q3, none assumed in Q4) flatter reported EPS, and the remaining roughly $480M of $1.0B paid is not probable under the company's recognition policy. A recovery would be upside; the loss of the tailwind is the baseline.

Valuation and consensus. The stock trades near 24x forward earnings against a 19x five-year average, and the Q4 consensus in the feed ($21.65B, $7.08) may be stale and above my arithmetic. Estimate cuts would add to pressure.

Working capital and credit. Inventory is up to $22.2B and receivables to $13.4B, with cash down to $7.9B. Cat Financial credit is healthy (past dues 1.31%) but the allowance rose to $332M (0.91%) and the provision is higher.

questions_for_management.question: Where does 'moderate' Q4 sales growth sit numerically, and how do you reconcile it with mid-to-high-teens full-year growth? Can you share the recast Q4 2025 base by segment, since rail moved to Resource Industries?

why.text: Nine-month sales are $58.64B and full-year guidance implies Q4 of $19.1–21.8B, which is hard to square with 'moderate'. The Q4 2025 segment base on the recast basis could not be sourced.

questions_for_management.question: What is the size of the rental fleet-loading lap in CI in Q4 versus the $1B dealer-inventory swing, and what sales-to-users growth do you assume for flat CI sales?

why.text: Management ties the roughly $1B headwind to the inventory change alone, and says fleet loading will contribute less to sales to users without sizing it. My arithmetic needs sales-to-users growth of about 9–10% for flat CI sales.

questions_for_management.question: What is the Q4 adjusted margin you are guiding to, what does 'near the bottom of the range' mean in dollars of sales at about $79B, and what drives the step-up in 2027?

why.text: Full-year margin is guided near the bottom while the target range is progressive in sales. A back-solve gives a Q4 range of roughly 18–19.5%, and each 25bp is about $0.09 of EPS.

questions_for_management.question: How much of the P&E backlog is firm versus frame-agreement or pipeline, what is the split between hyperscaler, colocation, IPP and oil and gas customers, and how are you monitoring customer funding and permitting?

why.text: The $78B backlog stretches to 2029–2030, book-to-bill slowed to about 1.3, and AI-funding and permitting concerns rose. Management declined to quantify hyperscaler mix.

questions_for_management.question: How large was the Q3 commissioning delay in mining, how much of Q4 RI growth relies on the catch-up and on dealer stocking versus sales to users, and what is the status of large-truck output against plan?

why.text: RI sales to users missed in Q3 (+4%, below expectations) and the Q4 'strong' sales-to-users guide depends on a catch-up of commissioning delays that management did not size. The CEO described ramp 'operational challenges and inefficiencies' and 'normal growing pains' without a timeline beyond saying they would be worked through.

questions_for_management.question: What is your assessment of the remaining roughly $480M of unrecorded IEEPA refunds, and is Caterpillar eligible for CAPE Phase 3? How will freight inflation from energy prices affect Q4 and 2027?

why.text: Recoveries fell from $392M to $128M, none are assumed in Q4, and Phase 3 only covers plaintiffs with court-ordered relief. Higher freight is an unquantified margin headwind.

data_gaps: The date and basis of the consensus in the feed ($21.65B revenue, $7.08 EPS, next report Jan 27, 2027) are unconfirmed. Press quotes a pre-call revenue consensus of $21.42B. A fresh post-print consensus pull is needed.

TIKR's $27.33 2026 'normalized EPS' consensus has no stated basis (adjusted or GAAP-like) and no stated capture time relative to the print; the implied Q4 is about $6.43 (adjusted basis) or $6.97 (GAAP basis).
The fact sheet's consensus growth rates (F.70, F.72) use Q3 2025 as the base rather than Q4 2025.

Q4 2025 segment figures on the recast basis (rail now in Resource Industries) could not be sourced. The CI base (about $6.93B) is derived from the 10-K and quarterly releases; the P&E base ($8.4–8.8B) and RI base ($4.15–4.35B) rest on an assumed Q4 2025 rail amount.
'Moderate' and 'strong' growth are undefined by management; the 5–10% band for 'moderate' and mid-teens or higher for 'strong' are my assumptions.

The Q3 2026 10-Q has not been filed or read, so Q3 share repurchases, average price, remaining authorization (about $7.2B by my estimate), Q3 segment balance-sheet detail and any footnote on the IEEPA receivable ($1.2B long-term plus $130M current at June 30, against about $520M booked in earnings) are unavailable.
